summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder, hypertension, and depression presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for several days. She had not been adjusting her sliding scale insulin due to a broken glucose meter and was only taking long-acting insulin. She was found in severe diabetic ketoacidosis with a glucose of 1162, pH of 7.06, and anion gap of 54. She was treated in the ICU with IV fluids, an insulin drip titrated up to 15 units/hour, and electrolyte management. Her course was complicated by transient hypotension requiring brief pressor support, acute kidney injury likely pre-renal from dehydration, and demand ischemia evidenced by ST depressions and a troponin peak of 0.28. She had a transient need for IV dextrose due to hypoglycemia during transition to subcutaneous insulin. Her kidney function improved with creatinine decreasing to 0.6, and she was restarted on lisinopril with addition of amlodipine for blood pressure control. She was discharged home with services on a reduced glargine dose, sliding scale insulin, aspirin, and close follow-up arranged with endocrinology, cardiology, and her outpatient substance use program.
